  • Innovation Partnership Awards recognize Magna’s collaboration with BMW on the EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps and with Jetour on the DHD Duo Hybrid Drive 
  • Automotive News names Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam a PACE Pilot Innovation to Watch 
  • New honors bring Magna’s all-time Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot recognitions to 16 

AURORA, Ontario, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Magna has received two 2026 Automotive News PACE Innovation Partnership Awards, recognizing its collaboration with BMW on the EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps and with Jetour on the DHD Duo Hybrid Drive system. Both technologies are in production. Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam, a pre-commercial bio-based seating material, was also named a 2026 PACE Pilot Innovation to Watch.  

The three awards show the breadth of Magna’s innovation capabilities across vehicle systems, from battery enclosure design and electrified powertrains to more sustainable seating materials. Each addresses a key industry challenge with technology built for real-world production and scale.

“This is a tremendous recognition of our teams and their ability to turn complex challenges into innovative solutions,” said Eric Wilds, Chief Strategy & Commercial Officer at Magna. “Whether it’s creating smarter ways to maximize space within a battery enclosure, delivering a flexible hybrid architecture or reducing the carbon footprint of essential materials, these innovations demonstrate what’s possible when Magna’s engineering and manufacturing expertise comes together with close customer collaboration.”

Magna’s EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps incorporates the company’s proprietary OptiForm™ stamping process to create near-rectangular, high-precision corners with tight radii. The approach increases available battery space by up to 10% while streamlining manufacturing. 

Magna’s DHD Duo is a scalable hybrid drive system designed to help automakers balance performance, efficiency and cost across multiple vehicle configurations. Now in series production, the system demonstrates Magna’s speed-to-market capabilities, moving complex, high-voltage propulsion technology from development to production at scale in less than 18 months. 

Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam integrates renewable resources into both the resin blend and the isocyanate components of polyurethane foam. The approach enables up to 20% renewable content while maintaining high-performance foam properties and reduces CO₂ generation by 18% compared to traditional polyurethane foam.  

The Automotive News PACE Awards recognize commercialized innovations from automotive suppliers for superior innovation, technological advancement and business performance, while PACE Pilot recognizes pre-commercial innovations with the potential to transform the automotive industry. With this year's three awards, Magna has now received 16 Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot recognitions over its history.

To learn more about Magna’s 2026 Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot winners and finalists, visit 5 Magna Innovations Named Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot Award Finalists.

ESTES PARK, CO / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Taranis Resources Inc. ("Taranis" or the "Company") [TSX.V:TRO][OTCQB:TNREF] is reporting on its exploration at the One O'Clock Target, located adjacent to Thor. This is the second of multiple targets explored by Taranis in 2026, the first being the Nortran Target (See News Release dated 11/05/2026). One O'Clock was initially identified using airborne geophysics and geological compilation work. Magneto-telluric conductive subsurface anomalies were found in an area associated with the Silver Cup Anticline. Field exploration in 2026 confirmed the presence of massive sulphide mineralization located at surface on the north side of the anticline.

Historical Description of Katinka

Sparse historical records indicate that most of the previous exploration work at Katinka was done prior to 1908, including two adits separated by 33m and an open cut. The records refer to a 3m wide quartz vein that strikes 070o northeasterly and dips 55o degrees south-southeast, hosting numerous veins of sphalerite. The vein was described as being in Ajax Quartzite near the apex of the Silver Cup Anticline. Both of the adits had caved in by 1955. Taranis did not locate the adits due to long abandonment and heavy overgrowth in the area. Nevertheless, other clues at the site confirmed that it was inhabited and worked by miners near the turn of the 20th century, and numerous high-grade surface samples were found in the vicinity of the historic location data. Indications of more recent workings in the vicinity of Katinka were also discovered, including a major abandoned concrete building foundation in what appears to be a mine dump.

2026 Katinka Exploration

Katinka is located 2.3 km east of the Thor Deposit and about 1.2 km northeast of the new mineral discovery at Borr. Taranis completed a number of reconnaissance exploration programs in this area including ground magnetic and VLF surveys, prospecting, and float/outcrop sampling. In-depth analysis of the One O'Clock target can be seen at http://taranisresources.com. Geological mapping in this area has shown the presence of a highly carbonaceous, overturned sedimentary package (interpreted to be the Sharon Creek Formation) located along the northeast limb of the Silver Cup Anticline. This highly-sheared and deformed rock unit is pyritic and characterized by 0.4-5.05 % total carbon and 3% sulfur (indicating 5.6% pyrite).

Taranis collected a number of grab samples found at surface downhill from the Katinka adits. The location of these samples is shown at the end of this News Release. Investors are cautioned that surface grab samples are selective by nature and the grades reported herein are not necessarily representative of the mineralization hosted at Katinka. The analytical results from grab samples are used to identify mineralized zones and guide future exploration, and should not be construed as indicating the presence of an economic mineral deposit. The Katinka metal signature contrasts sharply with Thor, being enriched in gold, silver and arsenic relative to the Thor deposit. It appears that mineralization at Katinka is relatively depleted in base metals (lead and zinc). The presence of such high levels of arsenic and also tin is noteworthy as it is indicative of proximity to an intrusive body, which is also inferred from the airborne geophysical data and further supported by drilling at Borr in 2026. Katinka contains many of the by-product metals found at Thor and Ajax (indium, cadmium, antimony and tin) indicating Katinka is part of the same, zoned, hydrothermal system. Katinka is also characterized by extremely high levels of sulphur (21.6%) indicating pyrite contents in the 37.5% range, making this type of lode an ideal target for geophysical surveys.

Location of Samples

The location and type of the Katinka samples discussed in this News Release appear at the end of the News Release per NI 43-101 disclosure guidelines (UTM Zone 11N, WGS84)

Importance of Katinka

Katinka is sandwiched between several historic epithermal deposits - Thor to the west - and the Nettie L./Ajax complex to the east. Katinka occurs directly on top of the Silver Cup Anticline along the northeast side of the Silver Cup Anticline where it is now steeply overturned and dips to the west-southwest. The contact between the Ajax Quartzite and Sharon Creek Formation is the host structure for the mineralization found at Nettie L. and Ajax, and this obviously extends northwest towards Katinka and Thor.

Conclusions

Katinka is a piece of the large hydrothermal system that extends for upwards of 5km that includes the Thor deposit, Nettie L. and Ajax Mines. They are linked by the Silver Cup Anticline. A metal-bearing hydrothermal system extends along the length of this structure, and has distinct metal zonation trends. Katinka is of interest owing to its high precious metal content, and lack of modern exploration. Additional work in the future would include detailed ground geophysical surveys and diamond drilling aimed at connecting Thor to the historic Nettie L. and Ajax Mines to the southeast.

Quality Control and Laboratory Methods

All samples for the Katinka surface sampling program were securely delivered to Actlabs in Kamloops, British Columbia. Analytical work was completed both at the Kamloops, and Ancaster, Ontario locations. Actlabs is ISO 17025 accredited. Rock Samples were analyzed using a combination of gold fire assay with mass spectrometry and INAA (Actlabs method FA-INAA, TD-MS and TD-ICP). Total carbon content was analyzed using method 4F (IR Method). Actlabs maintains a strict quality control methodology that includes internal standards and duplicate samples to ensure accuracy of results.

Qualified Person

Exploration activities at Thor were overseen by John Gardiner (P. Geo.), who is a Qualified Person under the meaning of Canadian National Instrument 43-101. John Gardiner is the principal of John J. Gardiner & Associates, LLC which operates in British Columbia under Firm Permit Number 1002256. Mr. Gardiner is the President and CEO of Taranis Resources Inc. and has reviewed and approved the comments contained within this News Release.

Update on Debt Settlement Submission

Taranis also announces that it is withdrawing its Submission to the TSX Venture Exchange regarding the proposed debt settlements announced on June 9, 2026.

  • New three-year strategy includes support for youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and pairs grant funding with employee volunteerism to deepen impact
  • Grant funding across three strategic commitments will support nonprofits serving communities in AZ, CT, FL, GA, IL, MO, NJ, PA, TN and TX
  • Applications open now through December 18 for nonprofits supporting patients and caregivers navigating complex health conditions

BLOOMFIELD, Conn., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Cigna Group (NYSE: CI) is deepening its community impact strategy with a focus on supporting youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and their caregivers. The strategy includes a three-year, $31.5 million commitment from The Cigna Group Foundation, the philanthropic arm of The Cigna Group, to support nonprofit organizations aligned to these areas. Informed by research identifying pressing community needs, the funding supports populations and areas where data suggests focused efforts can have a meaningful impact.

Experience the full interactive Multichannel News Release here: https://www.multivu.com/cigna/9433451-en-cigna-group-deepens-community-impact-strategy

Since The Cigna Group unveiled a refreshed approach to community engagement in 2024, the Foundation has invested more than $30 million in nearly 190 nonprofit organizations, with grant-funded projects reaching at least 321,000 people. The evolved strategy builds on that work, pairing grant funding with employee volunteerism, expertise and partnerships to help nonprofit organizations strengthen their impact in the communities they serve.

"Over the past several years, we've seen the tangible impact we can make when we invest in strong nonprofit partners and come together to help communities achieve better health and vitality," said Melissa Skottegaard, board chair of The Cigna Group Foundation. "We're building on what's working, bringing together funding, collaboration and the skills of our employee volunteers to address some of the most pressing health challenges facing communities across the street and around the world."

Three Strategic Commitments Support Health and Well-Being

Beginning in 2027, the Foundation will invest $31.5 million over three years across three strategic commitments addressing critical community needs.

  • Improving Youth Mental Health. Building on its longstanding commitment to youth mental health, the Foundation will invest $10.5 million over three years to continue supporting organizations that expand access to mental health support and resources, with a focus on meeting the growing needs of adolescents ages 12-18.
  • Enhancing Support for Veterans. The Foundation will deepen its support for veterans with a $10.5 million, three-year investment in programs that help veterans achieve greater stability through housing, employment and financial well-being initiatives.
  • Supporting Complex Care Patients. A new $10.5 million, three-year Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program will strengthen services for patients and caregivers, with initial grantmaking focused on autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, blood disorders, cancer, neurological conditions and rare diseases. Funding will help address non-clinical barriers to treatment, including care navigation, education, peer support, mental health resources and assistance with essential social needs.

"For people living with complex health conditions, managing their health requires ongoing clinical management, specialized treatment and coordination across multiple providers, treatments and support systems," said Dr. Amy Flaster, chief medical officer, The Cigna Group and board member, The Cigna Group Foundation. "I see firsthand how their needs can extend beyond medical treatment, whether it's understanding care options, finding emotional and peer support, or addressing practical needs that can make it harder to manage their health day to day."

"Community organizations can be a powerful source of support for people navigating complex health conditions," said Matt Perlberg, president of Evernorth Pharmacy & Care Delivery, executive vice president of Customer Innovation, and board member of The Cigna Group Foundation. "By helping patients and caregivers connect with resources and overcome barriers to care, these organizations can provide important support alongside essential medical treatment, helping people navigate their health and care journey."

Eligible nonprofit organizations can apply for the Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program through December 18 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

Funding Opportunities Across 10 States

Through its three strategic commitments, The Cigna Group Foundation will provide funding opportunities for nonprofit organizations serving communities in Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas.

Eligible nonprofit organizations may apply for two-year grants of $250,000 within the Foundation's three strategic commitment areas and defined grant program time periods, expanding community-based programs and services that help connect people with support services, overcome barriers and improve long-term health and well-being.

The Foundation will also continue supporting current grantees, including nonprofits supported through its Health Equity Impact Fund in Hartford, Connecticut, Memphis, Tennessee and St. Louis, Missouri.

Continuing National Partnership To Improve Youth Mental Health

The Cigna Group Foundation will continue its national partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, building on a shared commitment to improving youth mental health and well-being, now with a greater focus on supporting adolescents.

Since 2024, the partnership has helped expand trauma-informed training efforts to more than 90% of Clubs nationwide, reaching more than 11,000 staff members, while supporting new mental health resources now available at nearly 3,500 Club sites across the country. More than 1,600 young people have been reached through The Cigna Group employee volunteer activities, and employees have contributed more than 2,000 volunteer hours in support of local Clubs.

The partnership will continue to expand access to mental health resources, strengthen volunteer engagement with local Clubs and support the well-being of young people nationwide.

Employee Volunteerism Extends Community Impact

The Cigna Group's community impact strategy pairs financial investments from the Foundation with opportunities for employees to contribute their time and expertise through hands-on and skills-based volunteerism. Together, these efforts help nonprofit partners strengthen their organizations and extend the impact of the Foundation's investments beyond grant funding.

About The Cigna Group

The Cigna Group (NYSE:CI) is a global health company committed to creating a better future built on the vitality of every individual and every community. We relentlessly challenge ourselves to partner and innovate solutions for better health. The Cigna Group includes products and services marketed under Cigna Healthcare, Evernorth Health Services or its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group maintains sales capabilities in more than 30 countries and jurisdictions and has more than 180 million customer relationships around the world. Learn more at thecignagroup.com.

About The Cigna Group Foundation

The Cigna Group Foundation is a private foundation funded by contributions from The Cigna Group (NYSE: CI) and its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group Foundation aims to support, collaborate and convene with nonprofit organizations addressing society's greatest health challenges. In addition to increasing access to programs and care in geographies demonstrating significant need, the Foundation responds with humanitarian aid relief during critical times and strengthens colleagues' support of causes through matching donations and volunteer rewards. To learn more, visit www.thecignagroup.com/community.

Fuel Her Power provides practical nutrition guidance, drawing on more than 20 years of Herbalife's experience working alongside female athletes

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Herbalife today announced the launch of “Fuel Her Power,” a nutrition guide for active women designed to help better understand their unique nutrition needs and how to support energy, performance, recovery and overall wellness. The guide is part of Herbalife's Fuel Her initiative, which builds on more than 20 years of experience working alongside female athletes to make sports nutrition knowledge more accessible to women and girls at every level of sport and activity.

Fuel Her Power Nutrition Guide by Herbalife

Women's participation in sports continues to grow, yet nearly half of all female athletes aren't getting enough energy to fuel their performance1. With only 6% of athletic performance studies focused exclusively on women2, significant gaps remain in understanding women's unique fueling, recovery and performance needs. As a result, many women are left navigating nutrition decisions without guidance that reflects their physiology, life stages and athletic goals, with consequences that can impact energy, recovery, and long-term wellness.

“Fuel Her Power” translates sports nutrition science into practical guidance covering fueling, hydration, recovery, hormone health and women's evolving nutritional needs. It is designed to make insights gained through elite sport relevant to active females everywhere, whether they compete professionally, participate in recreational sports, train for personal goals or simply want to stay active and feel their best. The guide was officially introduced Nov. 12 during a Fuel Her event hosted by Herbalife and Break Sports in Los Angeles. The event brought together female athletes, nutrition experts and community members to celebrate the guide's release and advance the conversation around women's sports nutrition.

As part of the “Fuel Her Power” guide launch event, Herbalife also recognized four accomplished female athletes whose careers reflect the dedication, resilience and adaptability required to compete at the highest levels of sport. The athletes recognized included:

  • Heather Jackson: An ultra-trail runner, gravel cyclist and former elite triathlete, Jackson has six IRONMAN victories, 16 Half IRONMAN wins and four top-five finishes at the IRONMAN World Championship. Lecanemab showed favorable results on clinical assessment scores at 18 months, including among individuals with early Alzheimer's disease (AD) who were α-synuclein positive, a subgroup associated with higher amyloid burden and faster clinical decline

TOKYO and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB) announced today that findings from an analysis of lecanemab-irmb (generic name; U.S. brand name: LEQEMBI®) treatment and α-synuclein (α-Syn) co-pathology* in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) substudy of Clarity AD in early Alzheimer's disease (AD) were presented at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference, held in Boston and online.

In AD, α-Syn co-pathology may be present alongside amyloid beta (Aβ) and tau pathologies. α-Syn co-pathology may contribute to clinical heterogeneity and disease progression in AD, but its clinical relevance in patients with early AD receiving amyloid-targeting therapy remains unclear. In Clarity AD, lecanemab demonstrated statistically significant slowing of clinical decline in participants with early AD. This post hoc analysis evaluated the prevalence of α-Syn co-pathology and the clinical characteristics associated with α-Syn co-pathology and examined changes over time in clinical assessment scores in the lecanemab and placebo groups in the overall α-Syn-tested group and the α-Syn-positive (α-Syn+) group. These findings were presented in an oral presentation "Lecanemab Treatment and α-Synuclein Co-Pathology in the Clarity AD CSF Substudy" (OC50).

Overview of the Clarity AD CSF Substudy Analysis
A total of 623 CSF samples collected from Clarity AD participants at screening or baseline were assessed using the Amprion SYNTap seed amplification assay (SAA)**. α-Syn status was determined based on the detection of α-Syn seeds in CSF and used as an indicator of α-Syn co-pathology in the brain. Among the Aβ-positive (Aβ+) participants who were randomized to lecanemab or placebo and had α-Syn test results available, 400 were included in the α-Syn-tested group.

Key Findings

  • The prevalence of α-Syn pathology was higher among Aβ+ participants than among Aβ− participants.
    Analysis of the 623 CSF samples showed that the prevalence of α-Syn pathology was higher in the Aβ+ group than in the Aβ-negative (Aβ−) group (20.4% vs. 10.0%, respectively; p=0.001 by Pearson's chi-square test).
  • α-Syn+ participants had higher baseline amyloid burden and α-Syn co-pathology was associated with faster progression in early AD
    Among randomized participants with an evaluable baseline amyloid PET assessment, mean amyloid burden was 86 Centiloids (CL)*** in the α-Syn+ group and 67 CL in the α-Syn-negative (α-Syn−) group. The difference between groups was statistically significant (p=0.016 by ANCOVA). α-Syn+ was also associated with faster clinical decline over 18 months.
  • Lecanemab slowed clinical decline in both the overall α-Syn-tested group and the α-Syn+ group
    In this analysis, lecanemab showed a slowing of clinical decline at Month 18 compared with placebo in the overall α-Syn-tested group (n=400), similar to that observed in the overall Clarity AD population. In an exploratory post hoc analysis limited to the α-Syn+ group (n=82), lecanemab also showed a slowing of clinical decline at Month 18 compared with placebo. Specifically, the reduction in decline versus placebo, as measured by CDR-SB, was 27% in the overall Clarity AD population, 26% in the overall α-Syn-tested group, and 41% in the α-Syn+ group. As measured by ADAS-Cog14, the reduction was 26%, 45%, and 43%, respectively; as measured by ADCS MCI-ADL, it was 37%, 30%, and 43%, respectively.**** These findings suggest that lecanemab provides clinical benefit in individuals with α-Syn co-pathology.

Eisai serves as the lead for lecanemab's development and regulatory submissions globally, with both companies co-commercializing and co-promoting the product and Eisai having final decision-making authority

*

α-Synuclein (α-Syn) is a protein abundant in nerve cells that plays a role in signaling at synapses. Abnormally structured α-Syn can aggregate and form deposits called Lewy bodies. Lewy bodies are a pathological hallmark of Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. In AD, α-Syn-related pathology may coexist with amyloid- and tau-related pathology in the same individual. This is referred to as α-Syn co-pathology.

**

The Amprion SYNTap seed amplification assay (SAA) detects abnormally structured α-Syn aggregates in a sample by using them as seeds and amplifying their reaction in vitro.

***

The Centiloid (CL) scale standardizes brain amyloid burden measured by amyloid PET; higher values indicate greater amyloid burden. The scale is anchored at 0 CL (the mean in young adults without amyloid plaques) and 100 CL (the mean in people with moderate AD). The mean baseline value in Clarity AD was approximately 78 CL. Plaque negativity was defined as conversion to amyloid PET-negative status (<30 CL).

****

CDR-SB assesses overall clinical status, including cognitive and daily functioning; lower scores indicate better status. ADAS-Cog14 assesses cognitive function; lower scores indicate better status. ADCS MCI-ADL assesses daily functioning and independence in people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

    Lecanemab is the result of a strategic research alliance between Eisai and BioArctic. It is a humanized immunoglobulin gamma (IgG1) monoclonal antibody directed against aggregated soluble (protofibril) and insoluble forms of amyloid-beta (Aβ).

    Lecanemab has been approved in 53 countries and regions including Japan, the United States, China, Europe, South Korea, Taiwan, and Saudi Arabia, and is under regulatory review in 6 countries. Meeting will address Phase 2 study design and potential regulatory pathways for oral NEO212

CALABASAS, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NeOnc Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTHI) (“NeOnc” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for central nervous system (CNS) cancers, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has rescheduled the Company’s End-of-Phase 1 Type B meeting concerning oral NEO212 from the previously announced date of November 17, 2026, to Monday, November 23, 2026.

At the meeting, NeOnc intends to seek FDA feedback on its NEO212 clinical development program, including the proposed patient population, trial design, endpoints and dose selection for the Phase 2 portions of the NEO212-01 trial, as well as potential regulatory pathways for NEO212. The meeting provides an opportunity for discussion; its scheduling does not establish FDA agreement on a trial design or eventual approval of NEO212.

The meeting follows completion of the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of the NEO212-01 Phase 1/2 clinical trial. NeOnc previously reported that dose escalation was discontinued following a dose-limiting toxicity at 810 mg, administered once daily on Days 1 through 5 of a 28-day cycle, and that 610 mg was selected as the recommended Phase 2 dose. In September 2025, FDA authorized the Company to proceed with the Phase 2a and Phase 2b portions of NEO212-01.

NeOnc has also reported encouraging clinical activity observed during the Phase 1 portion of the trial. In one patient with recurrent IDH1 wild-type, MGMT-methylated glioblastoma (GBM), treatment with NEO212 resulted in a partial response, including an approximately 60% reduction in tumor size, followed by prolonged disease control lasting 21 treatment months. In a second patient with lung cancer metastatic to the brain who had previously received and progressed following multiple lines of therapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, treatment with NEO212 was associated with stable disease lasting approximately 16 months. While these individual patient outcomes do not establish efficacy and require confirmation in larger studies, they provide the clinical rationale for further evaluation of NEO212 in the Phase 2 portions of the NEO212-01 trial.

“We believe the durable activity NEO212 showed in Phase 1, together with a well-defined recommended Phase 2 dose, gives us a compelling foundation for the next stage of development,” said Amir F. Heshmatpour, Executive Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of NeOnc. “We look forward to discussing our Phase 2 plans with the FDA as we work to advance NEO212 for patients with CNS cancers who urgently need new options.”

Management anticipates hosting an investor webinar following issuance and receipt of the FDA’s official meeting minutes to discuss the Agency’s feedback and the Company’s anticipated next steps for the NEO212 development program. The Company expects to announce the webinar date, time and registration details separately.

About NEO212

NEO212 is an investigational oral conjugate of temozolomide and NEO100. It is being studied for CNS cancers, including recurrent glioblastoma. Preclinical studies support further evaluation of its potential activity and delivery characteristics; clinical efficacy and safety have not been established. NEO212 is being developed under an FDA investigational new drug application.

NeOnc Technologies Holdings, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for central nervous system cancers. Its investigational programs include intranasal NEO100 and oral NEO212. NEO212 has completed Phase 1 dose escalation and is advancing toward Phase 2 development. The ratings reflect Stewart’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management.

Stewart’s underwriting and operating metrics are expected to remain in line with industry averages despite the underlying economy and changes in interest rates, which could affect Stewart’s production and premium volume. Amid industry headwinds, Stewart’s ratings consider the group’s very strong levels of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), as well as its positive underwriting and investment results over the most recent five-year period. Stewart's earnings stability and business diversification is supported by its position as the fourth-largest title insurance writer in the United States, as well as its extensive geographic diversification across all 50 states, including its broad international presence. Stewart’s strategic acquisitions of companies that complement real estate closing solutions helps to mitigate its concentration as a monoline title insurance writer.

Negative rating action could occur if challenges from high interest rates and a slowing economy pose a significant decline in Stewart’s operating profitability and/or a material decline in its risk-adjusted capitalization levels.

This includes utilizing the "Restore.Earth" Physical Truth Infrastructure technology to push forward the movement to transform natural waste into innovative, eco-friendly solutions which restore soil health, conserve resources, and promote a greener planet."
